- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 30d forecast is below 75–78, adjust upward by 2–4% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7 days.
